articleTitle: Comparative analysis of the MPPT methods employed in the PV system, involving incremental conductance control and sliding mode control
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Energy Transition and Security (ICETS)
abstract: The objective of this research paper is to investigate diverse strategies for achieving optimal maximum power point tracking (MPPT) in photovoltaic (PV) systems. The research delves into the evaluation and comparison of two distinct MPPT techniques: incremental conductance (InC) and sliding mode control (SMC). A DC/DC boost converter is employed between the PV system and the load to facilitate the efficient transfer of the maximum available power. Conventional MPPT methods, such as InC, have shown limitations in detecting and accurately tracking the high point, resulting in a notable power loss. To address this issue, a proposed solution is the utilization of sliding mode control. This method has a number of benefits, including as accurate reference tracking, low distortion in current output, and resilience to changes in parameters. However, a challenge with this technique is the occurrence of pronounced oscillations during transitional periods. The results of simulation confirm that the outcomes achieved through The MPPT SMC outperforms the MPPT INC in relation to tracking the MPP, leading to reduced power losses. This suggests an improvement in the overall efficiency of the system. Additionally, the voltage and current are higher than in MPPT with InC. However, oscillations are more noticeable when using MPPT with SMC.

articleTitle: New Multi-band MIMO Antennas Based on SIW Technology : Design and Performance Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Energy Transition and Security (ICETS)
abstract: In telecommunication systems, the antenna is an important element for transmitting information between transmitter system and receiver system. To improve the performance of antennas in terms of coverage area, they are usually grouped into arrays. Generally, if the spacing between arrays elements is less than half a wavelength, a mutual coupling usually occurs, which reduces the adaptability of the system. It is therefore very difficult to install these elements in mobile units of limited size. In this paper, we propose new design of multi-band MIMO antenna based on Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SIW) technology. The model system is tested by simulation in HFSS environment with the conducting copper is produced on substrate of FR4-Epoxy, a dielectric of 4.4 at frequency 2 - 5 GHz. This paper is devoted to the presentation and analysis of the proposed antenna using SIW technology, and study theirs characteristics exactly in the frequency band [2 − 5GHz]. The simulations are performed using the HFSS simulation software.

articleTitle: Intelligent Energy Management Strategy For Multi-Sources Isolated DC-Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Energy Transition and Security (ICETS)
abstract: In recent years, DC microgrids have exhibited notable advantages over traditional counterparts, particularly in standalone and agricultural applications. This paper presents a standalone DC microgrid integrating multiple energy sources, energy storage systems, and power electronic converters. Emphasizing the region's substantial solar irradiation and wind potentials, the primary focus lies on Photovoltaic (PV) and Wind Turbine (WT) systems. Additionally, a Fuel Cell (FC) serves as a secondary power source to ensure energy continuity in critical scenarios. To effectively manage this complex system, an Intelligent Energy Management System (EMS) employing Fuzzy Logic Control (FLC) has been proposed. This FLC regulates the FC system's current reference based on the power discrepancy between the generation and demand sides while considering the battery's State of Charge (SOC). Utilizing the Matlab/Simulink environment, the results demonstrate the FLC's efficiency in managing the entire system, prolonging battery lifespan, and minimizing hydrogen (H2) consumption from the FC source.

articleTitle: Sensorless Torque Control of an Electric Vehicle Driven by an Open End Winding Induction Motor: An Experimental Study
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Energy Transition and Security (ICETS)
abstract: Electric Vehicles (EVs) are anticipated to play a pivotal role in addressing global climate change objectives and offering a solution for improved fuel efficiency. However, enhancing the performance, energy efficiency and cost remain the major challenges for EV technology. Identifying the operating points of the EVs motor drive system is crucial for optimizing its performance. Sensorless electric motor control for EVs is one of the promising research areas for cost reduction and performance improvement. This work’s primary objective is to develop, implement and validate experimentally a torque estimator based on Luenberger observer on an EV driven by an open-end winding induction motor (OEWIM) fed by two inverters. The proposed observer structure uses the complete OEWIM mathematical model. The rotor fluxes are estimated using the electrical model whilst the torque is observed using the mechanical model. This observer has been implemented using a board signified for a 1.5 kW OEWIM. The obtained experimental findings demonstrate the efficacy of the method put forward.

articleTitle: Fuzzy logic based speed control of indirect field oriented controlled doubly star open-end winding induction motor
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Energy Transition and Security (ICETS)
abstract: In this paper, a fuzzy logic (FLC) based speed control of indirect field oriented (IFOC) controlled doubly star open-end winding induction motor (DS-OEWIM) is presented. The windings of the DS-OEWIM are opened from both sides and fed by a dual voltage source inverter (VSI) for each stator. In addition, space vector modulation (SVM) technique was used to increase DC supply usage. Furthermore, the proportional and Integral controller (PI) was replaced by a fuzzy logic controller to deal with system uncertainties. The work introduced aims to enhance the speed control techniques by combining the multi-phase motor, multi-level inverters, and advanced controllers to improve motor robustness in the case of parameter variations and load disturbances. A numerical simulation was carried out using MATLAB / SIMULINK software.

Author Keywords: Doubly star open-end winding induction motor

articleTitle: Demonstrate the important role of the hybrid storage system in the FC-HEV application
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Energy Transition and Security (ICETS)
abstract: Fuel Cell Hybrid Electric Vehicles (FCEVs) emerge as optimal solutions for addressing the challenges of greenhouse gas emissions and conserving finite fossil fuel resources. Consequently researchers have embraced diverse innovative strategies to achieve optimal sizing and energy management in FC-HEVs, to enhance efficiency and reduce total operating costs. In this study, the Multi-Objective Particle Swarm Optimization (MOPSO) algorithm, implemented in MATLAB-16, is employed to model an application simulating a fuel cell hybrid electric vehicle. The in-house optimization code developed specifically for this Fuel Cell Hybrid Electric Vehicle (FC-HEV) application tackles the 3E challenges Efficiency, Economy, and Environment. By leveraging the MOPSO algorithm, the application minimizes a multi-objective function that incorporates key parameters such as investment cost, operating cost, and the weight of critical components, including the fuel cell, battery, and supercapacitor. Furthermore, this study utilizes the FC-HEV application to elucidate the impact of integrating a Hybrid Energy Storage System (HESS), composed of a battery and a supercapacitor, on the overall operating cost. The results notably demonstrate a 1.77% reduction in total operating costs when employing HESS, as compared to a scenario involving only the fuel cell and battery. This highlights the efficacy of HESS in achieving superior 3E outcomes for fuel-cell hybrid electric vehicles, emphasizing its potential to enhance efficiency, economic viability, and environmental sustainability.

articleTitle: Simulation and optimization of hybrid system (photovoltaic panel and diesel generator with energy storage) for Base Transceiver (BTS) station site located in southern Algeria
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Energy Transition and Security (ICETS)
abstract: Currently, diesel generators are the only source of electricity used by Algerian telecom sites isolated from the electrical grid. This production method has a number of drawbacks, including pollution, fuel costs, and greenhouse gas emissions. Isolated sites are justified in being cut off from the main network by their locations as well as their unique geographic and climatic features. Because diesel generators are readily available and dependable, they have been used the most despite these drawbacks. Therefore, the environment and the cost of producing energy would benefit from the combination of renewable energy sources and the diesel generator. Nevertheless, because the various energy sources run concurrently, this solution calls for extremely complex control algorithms. Three systems are being studied in this work: a photovoltaic generator, a storage system, and a diesel generator. High energy management performance has been attained by using a power management strategy among the various generators. To make up for the costs associated with installing the PV generator, a revised configuration for the isolated site power system was suggested.

articleTitle: Remote Supervision of Ambient Temperature Using Wi-Fi ESP8266 Controller Via MIT Android Application
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Energy Transition and Security (ICETS)
abstract: Over the past decade, significant advancements in electronics, computer science, and communications have propelled the evolution of embedded systems within the Internet of Things (IoT) domain. This paper focuses on the implementation of a remote temperature monitoring system, leveraging a Wi-Fi card integrated into a smartphone Android application. The development process involves utilizing the MIT App Inventor IDE, a user-friendly visual programming interface, along with the ESP8266 microcontroller for platform development. The temperature sensing capability is achieved through the integration of the LM35 sensor. The system enables real-time temperature monitoring and data acquisition, facilitating informed decision-making and timely responses to temperature variations. Through rigorous testing and evaluation, the effectiveness, accuracy, and reliability of the system are demonstrated. The combination of cost-effectiveness, ease of use, and widespread availability makes this solution suitable for a range of applications in various environments.

articleTitle: An efficient techniques for scheduling the hybrid electric vehicles energy management
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Energy Transition and Security (ICETS)
abstract: The problems of energy management in the power systems of electric vehicles (EVs) are among the difficulties facing the transportation world, especially with the hybridization of systems based renewable sources. The hybrid system in this work is an HEV containing a fuel cell (FC) as primary source, energy storage unit that is lithium battery, direct current (DC) generators, and second energy storage unit that is supercapacitors, each source connected with special power converters. This work studies a proposition for HEV, by integrating a DC generators as additional sources, and a deep neural network (DNN) in the energy management strategy (EMS).The proposed technique was responsible for reducing 30 % and 5% using DC generators and DNN-EMS respectively compared to state machine (SM), with improving the efficiency to 98.3%. The study’s objective is to show the impact of authors contributions based hard and soft techniques.

articleTitle: An Enhanced Neural Network Application for a Lithium-ion Battery Pack State-of-Health Estimator
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Energy Transition and Security (ICETS)
abstract: Evaluating the battery state of health (SOH) is a critical aspect of effective energy management. This study proposes the utilization of an artificial neural network (ANN) to create an SOH estimator for lithium-ion battery packs. To fine-tune the ANN, an experimental test was conducted under real conditions in a photovoltaic (PV) system, allowing for the identification of optimal weights. Various network topologies were developed and rigorously tested using MATLAB. The ANN, as a result, provides a highly accurate prediction of battery SOH by considering input parameters like voltage, current, charge/discharge current, and state of charge. The outcomes reveal a remarkably low mean squared error (MSE) of 1.4 x 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-5</sup>, underscoring the success of the ANN as a reliable approach.

articleTitle: Thermal modelling of connector with sand and connector without sand of the PV system connector under operating temperature in slar station of Kaberten-Adrar
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Energy Transition and Security (ICETS)
abstract: This The energy performance of photovoltaic solar power plants under real environmental conditions is the main objective of manufacturers and operators. Improving its performance requires continuous monitoring to examine and evaluate the condition of different parts of the station and identify various potential faults. In this study, we will highlight the aggressive effect of sand winds which blow in the presence of high temperature on the connectors which ensure the connection between the photovoltaic modules; we will model and evaluate the temperature of the 2 connectors, one with sand and the other without sand. Based on previous experimental data for two connectors in a thermal oven, each of them connected to a branch of an electrical circuit consisting of a DC power source, a shunt resistor and a DC lamp, bonded on each wall of the connector a thermocouple to measure the temperature, the modelling results show that the temperature of the connector with sand is higher than that without sand.

articleTitle: PEM Fuel Cell Electric Vehicle Controlled using PID controller
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Energy Transition and Security (ICETS)
abstract: The application of highly proton-conductive polymers is a significant technological development. These polymers function well over a wide range of temperatures because of their exceptional chemical and thermal resilience. Researchers have recently made great efforts to develop PEM fuel cells. As well as their use in vehicle systems in particular. This paper explains, understands, and models a proposed system for a proton exchange membrane fuel cell. Using the PID controller, the cell energy flow is controlled to a specific value according to the change in vehicle speed.In this paper, a PID control unit is designed to control hydrogen flow when there are fluctuations in vehicle speed. MATLAB/SIMULINK simulated the PEM fuel cell.The simulation results show that good control effects can be achieved using the PID controller system.

articleTitle: Input Output Linearization Control of DFIG based Wind Turbine
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Energy Transition and Security (ICETS)
abstract: In this article we present an non linear command wish is input output linearization control that used for controlling stator active, reactive powers of doubly induction generators (DFIG) based wind turbine and combined with PWM inverter. The robustness of this proposed controller demonstrated by the use of MATLAB-SIMULINK simulations.

articleTitle: Modeling and Simulation of a parabolic trough collector system for heating water under the Algerian Saharan climate condition: Tamanrasset area
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Energy Transition and Security (ICETS)
abstract: this article evaluates the thermal performance of a solar water heating system utilizing a parabolic trough concentrator (PTC). The main goal is to simulate PTC operational parameters using a single-dimensional numerical heat exchange analysis. The receiver, glass envelope, and fluid were segmented and energy balances derived for each section. The partial differential equations that regulate the system were discretized into algebraic formulations and solved concurrently. This study utilized MATLAB programming to solve for direct normal irradiance (DNI) using the Capderou model. DNI was modeled for the equinoxes (March 21st and September 21st) and solstices (June 21st and December 21st) based on recorded data, in order to examine seasonal variations, and water is used as a heat transfer medium. The Capderou model was chosen to calculate the solar radiation for a clear sky condition. The results proved that the selected area has a large amount of radiation, which makes it suitable for the study of the basin. The results also show the obtained water temperature value, which makes the model suitable for the production of hot water.

articleTitle: Integration of Photovoltaic, Lithium Battery, and Supercapacitor Technologies for Enhanced DC Voltage in Standalone Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Energy Transition and Security (ICETS)
abstract: In this study, photovoltaic (PV) panels, lithium battery storage systems, and supercapacitors are integrated to enhance the reliability and stability of standalone microgrids. Despite their importance, standalone microgrids face challenges relating to intermittent energy sources and voltage fluctuations in remote and off-grid areas.Using supercapacitors in conjunction with batteries can enhance power delivery and protect battery systems. This study investigates how supercapacitors can enhance energy efficiency, extend battery life, and ensure a robust power supply. The advantages of supercapacitor-battery hybrid systems, as well as mechanisms that ensure seamless energy management and battery protection, are explored in this study. In energy storage and electrification applications, these hybrid systems provide enhanced performance, reliability, and longevity by utilizing supercapacitors. It has been found that voltage stability and energy management have been significantly improved, indicating the potential for sustainable energy solutions in remote locations.

articleTitle: Elimination of Organic Polluant by Sand Filtration: The Case of Congo Red Dye
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Energy Transition and Security (ICETS)
abstract: The textile industry is among the primary causes of contaminated water, releasing harmful spills into the ecosystem. Because of their resistance to degradation in some cases, these spills pose considerable threats, not only to human health, but also to the equilibrium of ecosystems. This study aims to assess the viability of eliminating Congo Red (CR) dye by using the sand filtration method in the localities of BOUDA and El-METARFA, located in south-west Algeria. In addition to that, the impact analyzes of various parameters on the treatment approach was done in this study. The results obtained show that the optimum filter layer height for both types of sand is 30 cm. At this height, maximum Congo Red dye removal is achieved, resulting in removal rates exceeding 85% and 89% respectively for AL-METARFA and BOUDA sand blends. In addition, a removal rate of around 85% was observed for filters with a diameter of 200 μm or less. The results underline the disadvantages of smaller particle sizes, making the 200 μm filter the preferred choice for optimum performance. In conclusion, according to the results collected, it seems that the sand filtration method has remarkable technological potential when employed as a polishing stage in surface water treatment. This approach offers a promising solution for mitigating the damaging effects of textile dyes in the areas studied.

articleTitle: Evaluating MPPT Techniques: Optimizing Photovoltaic Systems Under Partial Shading Conditions
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Energy Transition and Security (ICETS)
abstract: In the burgeoning domain of renewable energy, photovoltaic (PV) systems have emerged as frontrunners, celebrated for their environmental sustainability and operational efficiency. Nevertheless, their performance could be more impervious to environmental vagaries, with partial shading presenting a formidable challenge. This study compares three Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) techniques: Incremental Conductance (IC), Perturb and Observe (PO), and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). Executing rigorous tests under consistent conditions, we aim to discern the most effective control method for PV systems navigating the complexities of partial shading. By delving into the nuances of this phenomenon, we endeavour to understand its ramifications and develop mitigative strategies. Our comprehensive study reveals that, under partial shading conditions, the PSO technique demonstrated robustness and efficiency in tracking the global maximum power point (GMPP), making it a superior choice for optimizing PV system performance in partially shaded environments. This research aims to enhance the resilience, efficiency, and lifespan of PV systems confronted with partial shading, offering invaluable insights for academic and industrial communities.

articleTitle: The impact of fractals on creeping flows: the "pile of sand" case study
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Energy Transition and Security (ICETS)
abstract: Because water may take on many various forms, erosion is more severe in areas that see higher levels of rainfall. Granular flow will be spoken about, and the main emphasis of the conversation will be on the fractalizing impact that water flow has on the surface of a sand pile. This effect causes fractal wrinkles to appear, and it also causes the sand grains to migrate. These events generate a variety of issues about their upbringing and development, the majority of which still need to be resolved to everyone’s satisfaction. In the end, we will discover that sand may assist us in resolving several mysteries about the topographical makeup of various regions.

articleTitle: Indirect solar drying of Saharan agricultural products using an intelligent system
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Energy Transition and Security (ICETS)
abstract: Solar drying of meat products has been practiced for thousands of years in many parts of the world. The advantage of this processing technique is that it extends the shelf life of meat products (conservation), making them safe to eat. Today, the methods of salting, smoking and drying are practically practiced just in time for occasion religious occasion.Solar drying has a number of advantages, the most important of which is that it is less costly, depending as it does on sunshine, unlike freezing. To this end, our aim is to develop a prototype of an improved indirect solar dryer. This involves precise adjustments with a few modifications to existing models, using an automatic tracking sensor to increase the prototype’s efficiency in order to reduce drying time and maintain the nutritional quality of the dried material. The impact of solar drying on the quality of meat products is studied through microbiological and biochemical analyses.

articleTitle: Experimental Validation of PV Module Modeling Based on Interpolation Approach in Outdoor Operating Conditions in the Southern Algerian Desert Regions
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Energy Transition and Security (ICETS)
abstract: Modelling and extracting the characteristics of a photovoltaic (PV) panel are crucial aspects in researching and advancing PV systems. PV cell modeling needs to take into account the actual irradiance spectrum data for each location under practical working conditions. Unfortunately, the nonlinear nature of the panel model makes it challenging to solve with analytical methods. In this study, a mathematically simple approach called bilinear interpolation was presented and used to model and simulate the I-V curves of PV modules in order to translate the I-V curves under all given radiation and temperature conditions. Under the climatic circumstances of the Algerian desert, the modeling results by bilinear interpolation were examined and compared with the experimental results. Whereas, this modeling method was applied to three different module technologies: mono-crystalline (ET Solar-75W), polycrystalline (PHOTOWATT PW500), and thin film (QS Solar 60W). The results of the bilinear interpolation approach validation were very satisfactory. Furthermore, the method enabled us to obtain updated STC characteristics values after many years of PV panel use; as a result, the studied approach was one of the best methods for studying photovoltaic panel degradation.

articleTitle: Modeling and Stress Analysis of a Wind Turbine Blade
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Energy Transition and Security (ICETS)
abstract: The paper focuses on the development and modelling of a 61.5 meter long wind turbine blade intended for use in a high wind speed location, with a specific layer thickness of 0.28 mm. As renewable energy sources, including wind energy, gain prominence in combating climate change and ensuring energy sustainability, understanding the performance of such structures becomes crucial. The research employs the COMSOL Multiphysics 6.0 software and specialized 3D modeling tools to meticulously craft a geometry model of the wind turbine blade. This intricate model is then subjected to Finite Element (FE) analysis using a layered shell interface based on layer-wise theory. The blade's design incorporates various materials: Carbon-epoxy, 10 layers of Glass-vinylester, 40 layers of PVC foam, and a single layer for specific purposes. Two main types of analyses are stationary and Eigenfrequency. The blade's structure is divided into 19 sections, each characterized by a distinct airfoil shape to optimize performance. The study delves into the gravitational, and centrifugal loads to comprehensively assess the blade's behavior. The distribution of Von Mises stress within the blade's skin and spar components under combined loads is a key focus. In the skin, the Von Mises stress distribution is reported at 3.07 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sup> N/m², while in the spar, the distribution reaches 2.47 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sup> N/m².

articleTitle: Elination of textile dyes using activated carbon from date stones
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Energy Transition and Security (ICETS)
abstract: This study consists in evaluating activated carbon was prepared from agricultural waste: date stones, for the decolorization of water contaminated by Malachite Green and Brilliant Green used in the activated state by studying the adsorption capacity of these dyes. After determining the effect of various factors influencing adsorption, such as pH, initial concentration and quantity of activated carbon, a kinetic and isotherm study of the adsorption was carried out. At the end of this study, it was established that the experimental results of adsorption of dyes on activated carbon are well represented by the pseudo-second order model, Langmuir model and the Freundlich model.

articleTitle: A Theoretical Study to Investigate in Perovskite-Based solar cells Single-Diode Model utilizing SCAPS-1D
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Energy Transition and Security (ICETS)
abstract: Perovskite solar cells have evolved as highly potential competitors for the future photovoltaic technology. However, various elements may hinder the effectiveness of these cells and influence their performance. In this study, we present a theoretical examination of the effect of thickness, temperature and parasitic resistances on perovskite solar cells performance. utilizing SCAPS-1D simulator, A regular planar configuration in five-layer FTO/TIO2 /MASnI3/ Cu2O/Au was adopted in this work. Our findings state that Photovoltaics Parameters such as Power Conversion Efficiency (PCE), Short circuit current density (Jsc), open circuit voltage (Voc) and Fill Factor (FF) are significantly affected. Our research offers valuable insights into the mechanisms underlying perovskite solar cells' performance and the factors that limit their efficiency. The findings may guide the enhancement of the manufacturing procedure for exceptionally effective perovskite solar cells.

articleTitle: A Technical and Economical Assessment of Hydrogen Production Potential from Solar Energy in Adrar, Algeria
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Energy Transition and Security (ICETS)
abstract: Hydrogen is an attractive fuel if it is produced from renewable energy sources (RES). The most ecological approache of green hydrogen generation, today, is the water electrolysis using RES. The present paper investigates the viability of hydrogen production from the solar energy resources of Adrar province (Lat: 27°52’N, Long: 0°17’W, Alt: 257m A.S.L) in Algeria using accurate monthly solar radiation mathematical model. Some of the key results exhibited that the daily average month solar energy varies from 3.93 Kwh to 8.79 Kwh in Adrar. Polycrystalline photovoltaic (PV) panel with 175 Wp rated power and proton exchange membrane (PEM) electrolyzer are employed. The required economic study is conducted to calculate the levelized cost of electricity (LCOE) and hydrogen (LCOH2). The final results reveal that the annual hydrogen production ranges between 3.06×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup> and 6.77×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup> Kg in 1 Km<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> surface. Furthermore, cost of hydrogen production from solar resources in Adrar is competitive, where the price of 1 Kg of hydrogen is 3.51 $.

articleTitle: A hybrid GWO-PSO algorithm for global MPP tracking in PV systems under PSCs
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Energy Transition and Security (ICETS)
abstract: Solar energy is rapidly gaining ground because of its sustainability, pollution-free nature, and cost-effectiveness. However, the efficiency of photovoltaic modules is affected by factors such as instant irradiation, temperature, and site-specific load properties. As a solution, MPPT strategies are employed to optimize module power extraction and reduce power losses. This study introduces an MPPT controller utilizing a hybrid GWO and PSO, specifically designed for PV systems operating under partial shading conditions PSCs.To assess the proposed algorithm, comparisons are made with both PSO and GWO algorithms to evaluate the performance of the hybrid method and perceive how the combination enhances tracking speed and efficiency compared to individual algorithms. Results indicate that the hybrid algorithm exhibits a minimum of 20% faster response time and superior tracking efficiency compared to PSO and GWO algorithms.

articleTitle: Power system stability improvement using shunt FACTS device controller based D-statcom
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Energy Transition and Security (ICETS)
abstract: The world's demand for energy is on the rise, which coincides with worldwide population and industrial expansion, particularly after the global economic recovery that followed the Corona pandemic. Because of this increasing energy demand, there are serious concerns about the reliability and stability of the electricity system. This research paper presents a modeling and investigation to improve the power system's stability under various operating conditions by employing the Flexible AC Transmission System (FACTS) technology. The MATLAB/SIMULINK/SIMPOWER-SYSTEM software package is used for simulate the test system. In this study, a 25-Kv distribution network's voltage is controlled using the A Distribution Static Synchronous Compensator (D-STATCOM). The D-statcom is a shunt device of the FACTS Groupe commonly used to improve the efficiency of the existing power system and the power system's stability. The results obtained indicate a significant improvement in the voltage stability of the simulation model in the presence of d-STATCOM.

articleTitle: Analysis of energy management and the environmental impact it has on electric vehicles: A comparative research and improvement opportunities
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Energy Transition and Security (ICETS)
abstract: This study examines energy management in electric vehicles (EVs) and its impact on the environment. EVs are a crucial component of the shift to greener mobility, but various interrelated issues influence their environmental effect and energy efficiency. This study will investigate the energy management practices used by current EVs, evaluate their effectiveness in energy use and CO2 emissions, and pinpoint areas for improvement in the upcoming electric vehicle generations.

articleTitle: An innovative clustering protocol based on the GRASP Algorithm for Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Energy Transition and Security (ICETS)
abstract: Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) are networks of several sensors positioned across the area to be monitored. For most sensor nodes, data routing uses a lot of energy. In order to increase the network's lifespan, it is critical that the sensors' energy be used efficiently. The WSN has a number of routing and power-saving techniques. In this paper, We suggest a brand-new procedure called MOD-GRASP (Modified Greedy Random Adaptive Search Procedure) designed to address the issue of optimizing energy usage in wireless sensor networks using the GRASP algorithm. The MOD-GRASP protocol seeks to minimize the amount of power used when relaying the collected data to the base station (SB). In the suggested protocol MOD-GRASP, a method for choosing the optimal Cluster Head (CH) in the WSN based on GRASP data is presented in order to increase the network's energy independence and, as a result, its lifespan. Experiments and comparative research have verified that our algorithm's application leads to a longer lifespan and less energy use than the LEACH methodology.

articleTitle: Impact study of radioactive release to the environment after hypothetical accident of AP1000 Nuclear Reactor
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Energy Transition and Security (ICETS)
abstract: The monitoring of pollutant emissions into the atmosphere is a major environmental issue for fossil and nuclear power plants. The industry emission to the atmosphere is indexed as the main cause of environmental pollution because of its significant production of waste deserves special attention. These consequences have worried the population, which has prompted the authorities of the countries to take an effective counter measures to control the various sources of pollution.For this purpose, this present work is oriented to the calculation of the core inventory and doses before and after an accident at the AP1000 reactor. The accident sequences take into account the destruction of all fuel elements. In order to calculate the Total Effective Doses (TED) in the air, the atmospheric dispersion of radionuclides was modeled using Health Physics HOTSPOT code version 3.1.2 enable the assessment of the contamination of individuals receiving doses.

articleTitle: Thermal Behavior of Photovoltaic Modules for Building Integration
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Energy Transition and Security (ICETS)
abstract: In Algeria, fossil energy occupies a preponderant place to satisfy the growing energy need. This represents a major problem for future generations due on the one hand to the depletion of this resource and on the other hand to global warming. According to the CEREFE report on energy transition - 2020 edition, the tertiary and residential building sector represents more than 40% of the country's total consumption [1]. BIPV represents an added value of sustainability, energy performance and promising economic prospects. It is an essential element of sustainable construction because it provides architectural functions such as waterproofing, insulation, solar protection and aesthetics. Knowing the operating temperature of the PV module is the key element for determining the temperature losses in a photovoltaic (PV) installation. In-situ, the temperature of the modules is difficult to measure, however, it is determined using models from the literature. The models used for the temperature estimation are programmed under Matlab. The objective of this work is the comparative study between different models of the literature, for the estimation of the temperature of the photovoltaic modules. The data used is extracted from a test bench developed to supply electricity to an office floor at the CDER.

articleTitle: Contribution to the MPPT control strategy for a photovoltaic system: a comparative study of PO, INC, and PSO
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Energy Transition and Security (ICETS)
abstract: Solar energy is the best energy solution now because it is a green energy, in addition to its efficiency. extracting this energy needs several techniques, one of those is solar panels, it is based on turning sunlight into electricity. Controlling maximum power point tracking (MPPT) and handling multiple optimization algorithms is an energetic and economic issue. This paper proposes a contribution to the MPPT control strategy for a photovoltaic system based on a comparative study of Perturb and Observe (P&O), Incremental Conductivity (INC), and particle swarm optimization (PSO). Partial shading reduces the delivered power and provides many local and global power points. Algorithms such as Perturb and Observe (P&O) and Incremental Conductivity (INC) generally may misjudge the MPP and fall in the local maximum power point (LMPP). The main goal is to track the maximum power point to achieve the best efficiency of the photovoltaic system. However, the method should provide optimal global maximum power point detection by analyzing the P-V characteristics. Furthermore, the simulation of choosing algorithms is tested by a boost converter with the PIC 16F877A on the ISIS Proteus platform. Simulation results indicate that the Perturb and Observe (P&O) and Incremental Conductivity (INC) algorithms do not map the global maximum power point (GMPP) whereas, the proposed PSO algorithm tends to the global maximum power point and ensures GMPP tracking under complex partial shading conditions.

articleTitle: Study of Automation and Supervision of the Boiler System in a Gas Turbine: Adrar Power Plant
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Energy Transition and Security (ICETS)
abstract: Automation and supervision play a very important role in industry today, as it is evidenced by its widespread presence in most modern industrial applications. Automation is available in a device called a programmable logic controller (PLC) that controls industrial processes. In this work, an improvement solution has been proposed based on the design of an automation and supervision system of a gas turbine boiler system in Adrar power plant using 7-300 PLC and Human-machine interface-based on WINCC Flexible. Several tasks have been added such as the alarm system in HMI to increase productivity and reduce human intervention.

articleTitle: Study of Solar Energy Gains in Algeria: Comparison of Monthly versus Annual Inclination
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Energy Transition and Security (ICETS)
abstract: The theoretical findings from this study reveal that the gain in extraterrestrial radiation between optimal monthly calibration and fixed annual calibration for 10 selected towns in Algeria is approximately 10%. Furthermore, experimental results obtained during a demonstration conducted in 2010 at the Renewable Energy Research Unit in the Saharan Medium (URER/Ms) headquarters in Adrar town demonstrate that the actual solar energy supply on the south-facing plane closely matches the optimal extraterrestrial contribution. The deviation is estimated to be only about 9% from a fixed yearly inclination throughout the year. These results serve as a fundamental reference for optimizing solar systems to achieve the desired performance levels during the design phase.

articleTitle: Analysis the operation of Smart Microgrid using the 'V2G' in the management of balance production and consumption
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Energy Transition and Security (ICETS)
abstract: In recent years, traditional energy systems have become inefficient and costly due to advances in control and communication technologies. Decentralized renewable energy production and storage systems are needed to meet demand fluctuations. However, integrating intermittent renewables like solar and wind poses grid stability challenges due to their weather-dependent variability. Intelligent systems that minimize distributed generation power fluctuations and conventional grid issues are required. This paper focuses on managing renewable intermittency in smart micro grids using Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) to balance production and consumption and minimize costs. An intelligent aggregator coordinates public and private V2G-enabled charging stations to inject or withdraw power according to daily needs. Simulation results analyzed various aspects related to smart grids and addressed efficiency issues in a V2G context, examining their roles in Microgrid regulation and production-consumption balance management.

articleTitle: Simulation and Study of the Effect of a Short-Circuit in a Transmission Line Bergeron Model Using EMTP and PSCAD Software
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Energy Transition and Security (ICETS)
abstract: The study of transient phenomena in electrical networks is a complex field, these phenomena lead to a particular focus on their immediate effects from their appearance until their disappearance or elimination. The duration of this type of fault thus generates a crucial and sometimes critical transitional period for the affected power networks, as it is generally very short, but which can have disastrous consequences up to the total collapse of the network (blackout).In this paper we used the Bergeron model transmission line supplies a resistive load to simulate by the two software of the transients EMTP and the PSCAD/EMTDC a single-phase short-circuit fault (phase C) appears in a 230kV this transmission line which, accompanied by the opening of a three-phase circuit breaker, and after elimination of this fault the circuit breaker closes, to have the consequences of this fault on the voltages of the nodes and the current transmitted in the Bergeron type overhead line, and to see the other side of the difference between the results obtained by the two transient simulation software in electrical networks.

articleTitle: Aerodynamic Analysis of an H-Type VAWT Rotor for Different Symmetrical NACA 00xx Airfoils
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Energy Transition and Security (ICETS)
abstract: Small-scale wind turbines, in particular VAWTs, are gaining in popularity in recent time. They provide, for example, omnidirectional wind power, and relatively easy installation. In this study, an H-type VAWT rotor (Known as H-Darrieus) was investigated numerically in order to compare four different symmetrical NACA 00xx blade airfoil profiles (NACA 0012, 0015, 0018 and 0021). CFD (Computational fluid dynamics) analyses were performed in ANSYS Fluent software, utilizing the Realizable k-epsilon turbulence model. The analysis included calculations of torque, lift and drag coefficients. Simulation results indicate that the H-type rotor with a NACA 0021 airfoil profile has the best aerodynamic performance.

articleTitle: RANS Simulation of two co-axially positioned HAWT under different thermal stratification conditions
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Energy Transition and Security (ICETS)
abstract: This paper proposes numerical method for aerodynamic performance predictions of Horizontal Axis Wind Turbines (HAWTs) immersed on Atmospheric Boundary Layer (ABL) flows under unstable, stable and neutral conditions. The flow field has been described using the three-dimensional Reynolds Averaged Navier Stokes (RANS) equations and the k-ϵ turbulence model with modified constants corresponding to ABL flows is considered. Based on Monin-Obukhov similarity, the ABL profiles under neutral and stratified conditions have been implemented into OpenFOAM where the flow over the fetch has been calculated through an in-house solver (ABLSolversimpleFoam) developed for steady-state turbulent flows. The immersed HAWT has been modeled using the actuator disk approach coupled to the Blade Element theory for the loads estimation. The obtained results have indicated that the velocity defect in the wake of a wind turbine is more significant in unstable than in stable thermal stability conditions. Consequently, significant variation of the wind turbine performances have been noticed; a power output drop of 37.64% and 13.67% being recorded for the second rotor placed in the wake of another and the first one respectively.

articleTitle: Solar drying types with fundamental physicochemical and microbiological characterizations applied to agricultural crops in the Adrar region, Algeria
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Energy Transition and Security (ICETS)
abstract: Solar drying, as a sustainable food preservation technique, has gained significant attention worldwide. This study explores the effect of solar drying on food security, with a focus on its impact in rural settings. In regions like rural Algeria, where agriculture plays a vital role in livelihoods, the implications of solar drying on food security are particularly relevant. Solar drying is known to reduce post-harvest losses by extending the shelf life of perishable foods. In the context of rural Algeria, this translates into greater food availability throughout the year. By preserving a wide range of crops, including fruits, vegetables, and grains, solar drying contributes to dietary diversification, reducing the risk of malnutrition. Furthermore, solar drying can serve as an income-generating activity for rural communities. Surplus dried food products can be sold locally, supplementing household incomes. This economic benefit enhances not only individual livelihoods but also community resilience. Solar drying also reduces reliance on food imports, contributing to national food security. In a changing climate, it offers a means of climate resilience by mitigating the effects of erratic rainfall patterns and water scarcity. It enables communities to store surplus crops during times of plenty for consumption during leaner periods. However, successful adoption of solar drying in rural Algeria requires addressing challenges such as initial investment costs, education and training, and ensuring adherence to food safety standards. It is essential to integrate solar drying into a broader agricultural and food security strategy, considering local contexts and needs.

articleTitle: Coherent Ballistic Phononic Transport at Slab Nanostructure in Surface Crystalline
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Energy Transition and Security (ICETS)
abstract: We investigate the scattering phenomenon at the non-uniform crystalline surface. The breakdown of translation symmetry caused by inhomogeneity gives rise to localized modes un its vicinity. The Newton equation and matching technique are used to study the phonon scattering mechanisms at the inhomogeneity. Together with the determination of the transmission and reflection probabilities and the elastic wave average transmittance across the defect, numerical results are presented over a broad range of scattering energies. This illustrates the differences in the scattering spectra of the softening, homogeneity, and hardening features of the perturbed defect. The coherent coupling between the propagating mode of the ideal waveguide and the localized modes formed by the defect results in fano resonances in the spectra. A detailed explanation is provided for a range of values of the elastic constants in the bulk and inhomogeneous domain. The system conductance is computed using the stimulating dimensionless frequencies and the characteristics of the system model.

articleTitle: Detection and isolation of inter-turn short circuit faults in induction machines
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Energy Transition and Security (ICETS)
abstract: Electrical machinery is becoming increasingly prevalent throughout modern society, making it imperative to enhance its reliability. These machines are susceptible to various electrical and mechanical faults and must be monitored continuously to ensure safe operation. The presence of any potential fault can result in unplanned downtime, requiring prompt assessment of any abnormal condition in rotating electrical machinery. It is widely acknowledged that the most common fault in these machines is the occurrence of ITSC in the stator. This type of malfunction accounts for 40% of the failures in the induction machine. The ITSC occurrence has hazardous effects on the machine and the associated electrical equipment. Therefore, early detection, along with an accurate isolation and severity estimation of these faults under all operational conditions, enhances the reliability and safety of industrial facilities. This article proposes an online method for detecting and isolating ITSC faults based on estimating the percentage of short-circuited turns in the stator winding. The estimation uses the Extended Kalman Filter, suitable for the nonlinear nature of asynchronous machine models. We conducted a numerical simulation in the MATLAB/SIMULINK environment to evaluate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed method. The simulation results demonstrate the efficiency of proposed scheme and ensure the detection and the isolation of the ITSC within the induction motor.

articleTitle: A Robust Adaptive Filtering Algorithm with Double Talk Detection in-Car Communication System
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Energy Transition and Security (ICETS)
abstract: This study focuses on solving the Acoustic Echo Cancellation (AEC) using adaptive filtering algorithms. The paper introduces an approach to incorporate a Double Talk Detection (DTD) mechanism based on Normalized Cross Correlation (NCC) into the Fast Normalized Least Mean Square (FNLMS) algorithm. This integrated algorithm exhibits enhanced convergence speed. The results from simulations validate the effectiveness of this approach in mitigating acoustic echo, particularly in scenarios involving real impulse responses, such as a car cabin impulse response.

articleTitle: Photovoltaic Power Supply of Mobile Fuel Station in The Algerian Sahara*
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Energy Transition and Security (ICETS)
abstract: Mobile service stations deployed in isolated areas in Algeria, use diesel generators to provide fuel pumps and accessory like lightening, AC, store, with electrical energy. However, since access to these sites is generally long and difficult, maintenance and fuel supply costs are very high. The objective of this work is to make a techno-economic balance of an autonomous photovoltaic system with storage batteries, for the supply of a mobile fuel station in a Saharan environment (site of Oued Namous (south-west of the Algeria)). In this study we determined the cost of production of photovoltaic kWh in the long term. Avantagouse result was been proved against classical mobile stations.

articleTitle: Effective Spline-GMPPT Approach Performance for Photovoltaic Systems under Uniform Irradiance and Partial Shading Conditions
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Energy Transition and Security (ICETS)
abstract: In the literature, there are several criteria techniques classified to achieve the point of maximum power tracking (MPPT) in photovoltaic (PV) power systems, such as accuracy, speed, and simplicity. These criteria are often trade-offs; in this case, the higher accuracy generally achieved at the expense of two other criteria: speed and simplicity.This contribution proposes a new technique based on the Spline-Global-MPPT approach to provide its reliability in multiple criteria as an accurate, fast, and simple technique to find the MPP of PV power generation systems under two cases, such as uniform irradiance and partial shading conditions (PSCs), in the total distorted characteristics of the PV string. A cubic spline interpolation approach has proposed in this method, which defines from a few simple points an approximate function.To localize the GMPP under standard (uniform) irradiance conditions, there are a huge number of interpolation-based approaches proposed in the literature. Unfortunately, this interpolation approach became incapable of detecting the point of the global maximum power (GMPP) under PSCs. The MPP of the system predicted by this new Spline-GMPPT method using a limited sample set of current and voltage, and it maintains this position as long as the external conditions stay unchanged. In the last part, the simulation results prove the reliability and robustness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Enhancing Nanogrid sustainability and cost-efficiency by Recovering household waste heat
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Energy Transition and Security (ICETS)
abstract: Nanogrids are Microgrids dedicated to produce low power forms of local energy. They are self-sufficient systems with one renewable energy generation, controls and, in most cases, energy storage. These systems are suitable to serve customers within a discrete footprint. Sources are usually solar PV or a wind turbine, and a battery for an autonomous operation.Since the operation cost of a Nanogrid is a key reason for the consumer to choose this environmental way for producing energy, we will present in this paper, an enhancement of cost operation by the participation of thermoelectric energy sources in providing energy to the domestic Nanogrid.The main idea is to recover the heat dissipated from all the electrical equipments installed in the house using a thermoelectric module using the Seebeck effect.A simulation was carried from ordinary house energy consumption data. The results highlight the contribution of this source and its positive impact on the general operation of the Nanogrid, and energy saving with zero cost investment.The simulation results obtained in this work are promising, and the simplicity of the concept will make it possible to generalize this form of energy to several microgrids.

articleTitle: An Improved PSO to Extract Unknown Parameters From a PV Panel
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Energy Transition and Security (ICETS)
abstract: This paper introduces a particle swarm optimization approach for determining the equivalent electrical model of a photovoltaic cell. Employing the particle swarm optimization algorithm as a tool, we efficiently extract model parameters by rapidly achieving a highly accurate global minimum solution. This is achieved through minimizing the Root-Mean-Square Error (RMSE) between experimental and theoretical characteristics. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness and speed of the proposed particle swarm optimization strategy in addressing these challenges.

articleTitle: Enhancing Frequency System Damping Efficiency via Optimal Integration of VRE in Grid
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Energy Transition and Security (ICETS)
abstract: This comprehensive study addresses the integration stability of photovoltaic (PV) systems in the SAIDA-NAAMA region of western Algeria, focusing on dynamic and static considerations. The research introduces an innovative approach, combining frequency stability analysis, optimal power flow control, and reactive power compensation within distributed power grids. Emphasizing the ESC PV Park in El-Abiodh-SidiCheikh, the primary goal is to enhance energy quality through dynamic stability. Implementation of maximum power point tracking (MPPT) techniques and compensating for reactive power variations demonstrates substantial progress, with up to a 24.72% reduction in active power losses observed under different load scenarios. Additionally, the study integrates reactive power control, utilizing NAAMA's static var compensator for the transmission network and localized compensations for the distribution network, ensuring voltage stability. Beyond reducing losses, these findings offer insights for increasing the ESC photovoltaic station's production capacity, contributing to Algeria's energy transition and green energy utilization. The proposed optimization algorithm proves effective in achieving multiple objectives, highlighting its potential for successful PV system integration into Algeria's national interconnection network (RIN), thus providing valuable contributions to the evolving energy landscape.

articleTitle: Identifying the ungiven parameters of photovoltaic modules using a novel optimization algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Energy Transition and Security (ICETS)
abstract: Efficiently optimizing photovoltaic (PV) systems is crucial for sustainable energy production. This study highlights the significance of precise parameter extraction and optimization to achieve optimal PV system performance within modern energy networks. PV module modeling, known for its nonlinear current-voltage behavior and limited cell datasheet information, presents inherent challenges. Recent research focuses on optimizing parameter extraction from the single diode model (SDM) using innovative algorithms. This paper introduces the Mountaineering Team Based Optimization (MTBO) algorithm for SDM parameter identification in PV modules. Through two simulation case studies, the algorithm’s efficacy is demonstrated, surpassing seven other established algorithms in terms of stability and accuracy. Obtained results emphasize the MTBO algorithm’s potential for enhancing PV system optimization and advancing sustainable energy practices.

articleTitle: Structural Static Analysis of a VAWT Blade under Operational and Extreme Wind Loads
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Energy Transition and Security (ICETS)
abstract: This paper deals with numerical static analysis of a straight symmetrical blade for 3KW VAWT (vertical-axis wind turbine). The calculations were performed in order to predict the maximum stress and displacement levels over the blade structure under various loading cases (.i.e. normal and extreme wind conditions). By using SOLIDWORKS commercial software, a finite element (FE) model of blade, which made up of Aluminum material, was analyzed. The results showed that the blade structure would perform adequately withstand extreme load conditions.

articleTitle: Performance study of organic solar cells based on P3HT:PCBM influenced by first order recombination and different active layer thicknesses
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Energy Transition and Security (ICETS)
abstract: In this study, the performance of organic solar cells (OSCs) utilizing poly(3-hexylthiophene):(6, 6)-phenyl C61 butyric acid methyl ester (P3HT:PCBM) material was investigated. The research employed optical and electrical modeling techniques, using the finite element method (FEM). The study explored the impact of varying the thickness of the active layer, consisting of P3HT: PCBM, as well as the influence of first-order recombination on the performance of organic solar cells (OSCs). The OSCs were constructed using a systematic structure of ITO / PEDOT PSS / P3HT: PCBM (with varying thickness) / Ca / Al. Optical simulations were employed to determine an optimal structure that enhances the absorption of light in the vicinity of the P3HT:PCBM active layer. Additionally, the distribution of electrons and holes within the active layer was investigated in the presence of first-order recombination effects. This increased absorption layer subsequently improved the electrical properties of the devices. The electrical investigation involved analyzing J-V curves under both illuminated and dark conditions. From these curves, key parameters such as short-circuit current density (Jsc), fill factor (FF), open voltage (Voc), and power conversion efficiency (PCE) were extracted. These measurements were performed under 100 mw/cm2 of Air Mass (A.M.) 1.5 Global solar conditions. The results revealed a notably high power conversion efficiency of 3.15 % for an active layer with a thickness of 200 nm.

articleTitle: Biodiesel production using a heterogeneous catalyst from Balanites aegyptiaca oil
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Energy Transition and Security (ICETS)
abstract: Researchers are currently working on the diversity of renewable energy sources. The Balanites aegyptiaca (desert date palm) plant is found in many parts of Asia and Africa, including southern Algeria in the wilayas of Adrar, Bordj-Badji Mokhtar and Tamanghast. In this work, we were able to produce biodiesel from Balanites aegyptiaca fruits oil. The oil was extracted by the Soxhlet method, using hexane as solvent. The biodiesel produced by the transesterification reaction consists of adding hexane and heterogeneous catalyst, namely the husk of the fruit of Balanites aegyptiaca, to the oil, with a yield of 91.4%. The biodiesel produced was characterized by physicochemical methods, namely density, viscosity, refractive index, pour point and flash point. The characterization values obtained are very close to international standards.

articleTitle: Modeling, simulation and analysis of the input climat parameter effect on the photovoltaic panel
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Energy Transition and Security (ICETS)
abstract: This paper presents a Simulink model of a solar panel. The model is utilized to analyze the effects of changing external parameters on the panel's operation. Radiation and temperature are the parameters analyzed. It was observed that variations in input climate parameters influence the external parameters and characteristics of the photovoltaic panel. The results demonstrate that increasing temperature reduces the open-circuit voltage of the photovoltaic panel. In contrast, elevating solar irradiance results in a higher short circuit current.

articleTitle: Meta-Heuristics Optimization Based MPPT control of Wind Energy Conversion System with Permanent Magnet Synchronous Generator
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Energy Transition and Security (ICETS)
abstract: This work aims to improve control and optimization of a renewable power system comprising a direct-drive H-Darrieus wind turbine (DDH-DWT) coupled to a permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM). The goal is maximizing wind energy extraction using advanced optimization methods.The control challenge is posed as an optimization problem, where the difficulty lies in finding the ideal controller parameters. To tackle this, we implement the metaheuristic Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO) algorithm. GWO mimics wolf hunting behaviors to efficiently pinpoint global optima.Simulations verify the GWO-optimized controller's effectiveness - it increases wind power generation through improved tracking and adaptation under variable conditions. Results validate GWO's optimization capabilities for boosting renewable energy harvesting via control. The approach succeeds in boosting power output from the H-DWT system while maintaining robust performance under fluctuating wind conditions. The self-adaptive GWO algorithm provides precision monitoring and optimization capabilities.The results obtained from our investigation underscore the efficacy of the proposed control strategy in terms of its monitoring capabilities and robustness.

articleTitle: Backstepping control of a wind turbine connected to the grid (base on DFIG)
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Energy Transition and Security (ICETS)
abstract: This study discusses the use of the backstepping method to control a nonlinear system and design a stable controller.The doubly fed induction generator (DFIG) is a nonlinear system, and its integration into a wind power system connected to the grid will complicate the control of the global system.Thus, the stabilization of the system requires a recursive method, which is provided in the backstepping method.The reactive power and electromagnetic torque are controlled by the rotor side converter (RSC) through the use of a nonlinear controller that is based on the backstepping technique.It is used by the grid side converter (GSC) to control the power switched with the grid and to regulate the DC-bus voltage.The simulation tests are done using the program MATLAB/Simulink to validate the efficiency of the technique in controlling the system.

articleTitle: Improved Harmonic Mitigation with a SAP Filter Connected to a Renewable Energy Source using a Novel ANN Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Energy Transition and Security (ICETS)
abstract: The quality of electrical power can be compromised by a range of factors, including harmonic distortion resulting from non-linear loads. To counteract current harmonics generated by these non-linear loads, a shunt active power filter (SAPF) is employed. This study introduces a novel algorithm for detecting reference harmonic currents within SAPF connected to a two-level voltage converter, utilizing the ANN algorithm for this purpose, and PWM (Pulse Width Modulation) for pulse generation. The current control strategy incorporates an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) method to enhance power quality by compensating for harmonics and reactive power demanded by non-linear loads. This research involves a comparison between the performance of a SAPF using the ANN algorithm and that using the instantaneous P/Q theory. Through simulation analyses conducted across three distinct scenarios, various system parameters are evaluated, including source current with and without SAPF using the two different algorithms, ANN and PQ. Furthermore. The primary objective of this research is to offer valuable insights into the effectiveness of the ANN algorithm in improving power quality, so reducing harmonic pollution.

articleTitle: Robust Control H∞ to the Wind System
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Energy Transition and Security (ICETS)
abstract: This work presents the design and implementation of a robust H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> control of the wind system based on a double-feed asynchronous generator "GADA". The interest in the GADA is due to its ability to provide active power by the stator and by the rotor according to its mode of operation. The usual GADA topology adopted in this work is to connect the stator directly to the grid, while the rotor connects through two two-level three-phase converters. Application of robust H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> control technique to wind power system with the robustness test vis-à-vis the variations of the electrical and mechanical parameters of the machine, show considerable improvements in the dynamic performance and a great stability robustness of the system studied.

articleTitle: Analysis study and simulation of a real mono crystalline photovoltaic plant in desert area
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Energy Transition and Security (ICETS)
abstract: In this paper, the monocrystalline photovoltaic field located in the Oued Nechou site in Ghardaia (Algeria), has been analyzed and simulated. This PV plant, panel, cellule, and array were analyzed and simulated in various cases and in STC and in order to better understand its performances. In addition, a simulation of a monocrystalline PV plant using actual climate data has been conducted to assess the PV plant and determine its potential of solar energy production. The obtained results indicate that the temperature and sun irradiation affect the performance of the photovoltaic system, which results in fluctuations in both the performance ratio and the amount of electrical energy produced. Additionally, they show that the solar potential is good, which permits the production of energy even the variations of environment conditions. This supports the installation of additional PV plants in the region.

articleTitle: Renewable energies in the twenty-first century : A global-view
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Energy Transition and Security (ICETS)
abstract: This paper present one of the important issues in these decades: Renewable Energies, it shows an upward trend of growth in the 21st century (from 2000 to 2022), mostly in this last five years especially with COVID-19 and world’s politics events. That’s why major research, development and implementation efforts around the world focus on sustainable energy sources.This overview is based on an effective study of the future energy sources; as we knew the five main renewable energy generation technologies are: the hydro, the wind, the solar, the biomass and the geothermal energy, so in this review, we will look at data on major renewable energy generation across the world's continents in the recent period from 1990 to 2022; its big changes and its increases.

articleTitle: Investigation of attenuation coefficients of some building materials
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Energy Transition and Security (ICETS)
abstract: Recent years have seen a rise in the usage of radioactive elements, both for military and medical purposes. This has led us to look for radiation shielding materials that are more effective and efficient than lead Pb 82, which is costly, heavy, and toxic. Our topic will be devoted to examining the characteristics of free, readily available, local, and natural materials like clay and sand. These days, bricks and cement are the most used building materials. After calculating the attenuation coefficients for each material, we compared them to one another and to the lead attenuation coefficient as a benchmark. To do this, a WinXcom application was used.

articleTitle: Extraction of electrical parameters for one diode photovoltaic model using iterative chaotic AEO optimization algorithm)
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Energy Transition and Security (ICETS)
abstract: Most of the time, photovoltaic (PV) cells' datasheets don't list their model factors. Getting the right PV settings is a very important problem that experts are very interested in. There is a new way to guess the one diode model (ODM) parameters in this study. It is called the iterative chaotic Aeo-1 optimization method (ICAeo-1). The current method uses only addition and multiplication to make the original AEO-1 algorithm better at exploring. It does this through a repeated map-based learning process. The Root-Mean-Square-Error (RMSE) numbers get better, which is a good sign. It can be seen that the ICAeo-1 algorithm is better at predicting the PV parameters than a lot of other well-known algorithms when it comes to being accurate and stable.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of a VSC-HVDC System Interlinked with a Passive Network
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Energy Transition and Security (ICETS)
abstract: Every day, power transmission encounters numerous difficulties. The demand for power has surged, and because of population growth, urbanization, environmental concerns, and other factors, it is become harder to choose the best route for new lines. For long distances, high-voltage direct current (HVDC) transmission systems are more cost-effective than high-voltage alternating current (HVAC) transmission systems. In this paper, a Voltage Source Converter (VSC)-based HVDC link model is developed using MATLAB/SIMULINK. This relatively new technology has a number of benefits, including speed and the ability to control both active and reactive power across a 300-kilometer passive network of 15 KV and 50 Hz from an AC system operating at 400kV and 50 Hz. The outcomes from the system under study demonstrate that high voltage direct current connections enhance the reliability and stability of electrical networks and energy quality.

Author Keywords: High Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) Transmission - Voltage Source Converters (VSC) – Interconnecting Power Grids

articleTitle: STATCOM contribution to improving the stability of power grids -Application Adrar Algeria_network-
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Energy Transition and Security (ICETS)
abstract: This paper deals with the problem of compensation of reactive power into the grid as well as the contribution of STATCOM to network stability. The simulation model of STATCOM with its control laws was made in the universe MATLAB .The first network simulation was made in the healthy state, then a three-phase fault is applied and the model developed STATCOM is inserted in a real network in southern Algeria (Adrar Area) and the results are exposed. The model developed takes into account the dynamic behavior of the structure of the STATCOM, and brings supplemental wealth for the dynamic study of the network and its stability.

articleTitle: Cooling of a Coil Integrated in a Micro-Converter by Air Jet
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Energy Transition and Security (ICETS)
abstract: The object of this paper is the study of the influence on the one hand of the non-isothermal vertical laminar flow of the ambient air on the thermal behavior of a circular planar inductor with 3 turns and on the other hand on its cooling. The mathematical model is composed of the equations of continuity of air flow, and conservation of energy or even heat. The resolution of these equations was carried out by the finite element method using Comsol Multiphysics software. The field of study is a cubic cavity in which the coil is introduced. The vertical air field is assumed to be incompressible. The coil is considered as an obstacle for the axial flow. The results obtained on the thermal behavior of the coil demonstrated that the rate of cooling by ventilation increases with the increase in the intensity of electric current without the need for cooling of the discharged air.

articleTitle: Realization and implementation of an experimental anaerobic digestion device of agricultural waste of animal origin
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Energy Transition and Security (ICETS)
abstract: The methane biogas extracted from the fermentation of agricultural waste constitutes an immense source of renewable cogeneration energy which can be very well valued in Algeria. In this work, we present an experimental study on the anaerobic digestion of agricultural waste of animal origin. The waste targeted consists mainly of cow dung 90%, straw and residues of animal feed 10%. The practical task of our work represents the realization of the experimental device intended for the fermentation of the selected agricultural waste, and then its implementation in the digestion phase. As results, we concluded that animal waste is highly recoverable by anaerobic digestion, which offers better waste management on site and at lower cost. The increase in temperature accelerates the fermentation process and ultimately produces, in addition to methane, a fertilizing waste, inert and energetically stable.

articleTitle: A Review of some LEACH Optimization Protocols for Wireless Sensor Network Clustering
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Energy Transition and Security (ICETS)
abstract: The range of using wireless sensor networks is very wide as its application includes most fields. Because of the impact of communication costs on node power consumption, this sort of network has restricted node capacity and a short lifespan. Sensor nodes in wireless sensor networks rely on their mostly non-rechargeable batteries to monitor, collect information and send it back to the Sink, via various techniques for routing. remarkably efficient and extensively used routing protocol is LEACH. as it is based on a hierarchical grouping of nodes. However, it suffers from some drawbacks. In this article, we attempt to address the LEACH protocol and a comparative presentation of some of the improvements that have come in the literature. Finally, we offer proposals for enhancing this technique.

articleTitle: Mathematic model for photovoltaic module under fault conditions
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Energy Transition and Security (ICETS)
abstract: It is frequently difficult to avoid photovoltaic generator problems that reduce performance and energy production. Aside from the deviations of the curve (Current-Voltage) caused by inserting indicators for each Component, depending on the nature of the faults (shading, soiling, mismatch, and by-pass diode faults), this study employs a novel technique to represent the causal relationship between faults and afflicted components. The symptoms and deviations of the Current-Voltage were simulated using MATLAB Simulink. As a result, the impact of faults on components Iph, Rs, Rsh, and bpd was identified. Whereas the modelling of PV generator behaviour is based on the type of fault (shading, soiling, mismatch, and bpd faults), this is the foundation of diagnosing and identifying all circumstances of safety and defects.

articleTitle: Experimental Investigation of the Energy Efficiency of Earth Brick from the Aoulef Region in Algeria
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Energy Transition and Security (ICETS)
abstract: Clay brick is used all over the world, because it is an ancient building material, and its strength and elasticity vary depending on its water content and the type of additives to it .
